minutes.headline: Green Task Force heard a utility heat pump consult for Turkey Hill and discussed the risky cost of the primary school mini-split grant project.
minutes.summary: Utility staff walked the group through a Mass Save heat pump consultation for Turkey Hill, covering weatherization, contractor quotes, rebates and timelines. Members then discussed the primary school mini-split grant project, whose cost is uncertain and may exceed the funds on hand, and the tight close-out timeline. The March 3 minutes were approved by voice vote and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

attendees.role: presenter, program manager, utility commercial support team

votes.motion: Adjourn the meeting; roll call taken.

budget_items.what_was_said: Presenter said utilities typically cover a share of weatherization for municipal buildings, starting with a no cost assessment.
Rebates are paid per ton; air source, VRF and geothermal rates differ, geothermal highest.
Federal credit would come to the school as a direct payment for eligible geothermal systems.

budget_items.topic: Primary school mini-split project cost and shortfall
budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked whether the project figure is committed, noting the town could be short; the vendor will not firmly commit to a price. Tariffs may raise costs.
Chair said the project is largely grant funded and the school would give that up if it dropped it.

budget_items.topic: Grant writing services in town manager budget
budget_items.what_was_said: Vice chair said the town manager put grant writing and grant management services back in the budget.
Vice chair said the town turned back grant money in one case because it lacked the balance for the project.
Speaker said solar credits are poorly allocated, with some buildings holding credits while another pays heavily.

budget_items.topic: Capital plan amendment for primary school
budget_items.what_was_said: School committee voted to withdraw capital projects from the town manager's plan and replace them with an equal amount for the mini-split project, pending town meeting.

decisions.decision: Utility staff to connect the town with the National Grid municipal rep for a weatherization audit and to follow up on the contractor tool.
Chair to contact the town manager the next morning about next steps on the primary school project.
Group agreed to look at getting quotes from other contractors, who must be on the approved list.
Next meeting tentatively set for the first Monday in May, by Zoom.

The Turkey Hill heat pump and weatherization work may be partly covered by utility programs and rebates, which could reduce what the town pays for municipal building upgrades.
